policy: The copied v0.1 experience is binding. Later logic may enter only through a narrowly tested adapter or runtime boundary. No experience file may change without a named bug and before-after browser proof.
allowedPorts: canonical Next runtime and exact-origin/session repair
sanitized current-run and Recorded Runs read model
forbiddenPorts: v0.2 rail geometry or large node composition
a cloned or fabricated provider approval page

approval.scope: The approved recovery repairs preserve the v0.1 composition while repairing the exact named runtime, same-session return, exact Recorded Run selection, six-subject Story Lab, and evidence-linked rail motion.

approvedBoundaryDeltas.reason: Make the pinned Linux Node 22.23.2 Next runtime at http://onsale-v01.localhost:4310 the exact default, retain one anonymous session and current-order pointer through provider return, and resume on clean /checkout without trusting query state.
approvedBoundaryDeltas.claimBoundary: This is deterministic local runtime and browser-origin proof. It does not prove a live provider return, hosted database continuity, deployment, or human comprehension.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the accepted buyer composition while using the packaged event hero and linking a terminal result to its exact retained run when one exists.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Remove the remote hero dependency, preserve the event hierarchy, announce the completed current run, and route the result action to /flows?run=<opaque-ref> without falling back to another run.

proof.claimBoundary: The browser receipt proves the current event render and exact local origin. The intercepted Next browser gate owns exact-run no-fallback behavior.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Preserve the compact six-actor topology and singular amber token while projecting preparation, Pay, retrieve, and ticket handoffs from retained authority changes.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Restore the authored one-token sequence for checkout preparation, buyer Pay activation, same-payment retrieve, and exact one-charge ticket fulfillment without changing the approved trace geometry.

proof.claimBoundary: The browser receipt proves the current rail renders without overflow or runtime errors. Component gates prove the one-token state contract. Motion-media capture remains blocked.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Recorded Runs uses only the sanitized same-session read model; exact-run requests resolve to that run or a target-specific error with no fallback.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Replace compile-time Previous Runs with the read-only ledger, current-run completion signal, cursor-safe merge, and exact opaque run selection while keeping Story Lab separate.

proof.claimBoundary: The current browser receipt proves the Recorded Runs surface. Hosted Neon history remains blocked and no fixture may substitute for an unavailable ledger.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Expose exactly the six accepted Story Lab IDs and keep all replay state deterministic and simulation-only.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Restore the approved six-subject taxonomy and make replay transitions accept the selected retained or simulated flow without laundering simulation into Recorded Runs.

proof.claimBoundary: This proves a local deterministic Story Lab surface. It is not provider, merchant, or performance evidence.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the accepted sharp cobalt workbench while making refresh and pagination actions legible and stateful.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Add visible hover and disabled states for the Recorded Runs refresh and load-more actions without changing the page composition or introducing a new styling system.

proof.claimBoundary: The receipt proves current desktop containment and zero browser errors. Named-human comprehension and accessibility remain blocked.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Render the retained-run skeleton on the first paint instead of flashing an unavailable-ledger error before the owned read starts.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The user observed a retry and no-selection error flashing before the useful skeleton. A typed loading seed now owns the first render; real request failures still retain their recovery action.

proof.claimBoundary: This proves the initial rendered markup. The combined named-runtime browser gate remains the final visual authority.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the existing quiet ledger skeleton while adding one neutral line that explains the retained evidence wait.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The loading state now says Loading runs and Awaiting retained payment evidence without adding a card, spinner, or alternate visual language.

proof.claimBoundary: This is a narrow loading-state style proof; responsive visual proof is rerun on the combined candidate.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the accepted six Story Lab subjects while naming each by the payment decision and consequence it teaches.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Internal labels such as Confirmed payment and Method versus connector lab did not tell a reviewer why the story exists. The six IDs, proof classes, evidence, steps, and replay behavior remain unchanged.

proof.claimBoundary: This proves the exact six labels and unchanged deterministic catalog; final visual wrapping is checked on the combined browser candidate.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Explain that Story Lab contains six payment decisions and that each selected state is present because its business consequence matters.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Replace generic Curated demos metadata with the reader job without changing workbench structure or replay controls.

proof.claimBoundary: This is a content-hierarchy change only; browser proof owns final legibility.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Let the official Hyperswitch fullscreen iframe escape the checkout card and cover the ONSALE viewport without changing provider action logic.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The completed entrance animation retained an identity transform and the checkout card hid overflow, creating a containing and clipping block for Hyperswitch's position-fixed fullscreen iframe. Backwards fill preserves the entrance but releases the transform; only the provider card permits overflow.

proof.claimBoundary: This proves ONSALE no longer clips a fullscreen iframe. The provider-owned inner card and approval controls remain cross-origin and are not restyled or simulated.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Open the complete Flows ledger from a fulfilled ticket instead of coupling the buyer action to an exact-run query.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The prototype should always show the full run list. The fulfilled buyer action now uses the same stable /flows destination as the header.

proof.claimBoundary: This proves the buyer link destination and label. It does not change run capture, ledger reads, or payment completion.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Use one stable /flows action in the payment rail rather than changing its destination by checkout state or run availability.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: A generic ledger destination preserves the full Previous Runs list and removes a fragile presentation-only query coupling.

proof.claimBoundary: This proves the rail link is stable. Trace facts, topology, motion, and replay controls are unchanged.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep a completed buyer on the event surface when sale-entry controls are pressed and direct them to the saved ticket and explicit reset action.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The eligibility and seat screens intentionally do not render while a durable checkout snapshot exists. Guarding both entry callbacks prevents the resulting blank state and explains the existing Buy Another Ticket reset path.

proof.claimBoundary: This proves both sale-entry controls remain on the event surface for a fulfilled order. The existing reset request, session rotation, payment, and ticket issuance logic are unchanged.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the stable /flows destination while naming the fulfilled-order action by the recorded payment the reviewer expects to inspect.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Open Flows described the destination but not the reviewer job. The requested label restores the payment-specific meaning without restoring the fragile run query.

proof.claimBoundary: The label and /flows href are covered. Recorded-run selection and ledger contents are unchanged.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Offer the fulfilled buyer a direct Buy Another Ticket action beside View Your Tickets on the saved-order banner.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: A buyer returning home after fulfillment should not have to reopen the ticket wallet to discover the existing reset path. The banner now invokes the same guarded reset operation directly.

proof.claimBoundary: The banner action and one reset request are covered. The server continues to preserve the anonymous history identity while clearing the active order pointer.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep View Your Tickets and Buy Another Ticket adjacent, legible, and visually distinct at desktop and narrow widths.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The primary action remains filled while the destructive-to-current-progress reset action is outlined; both retain the existing control size contract.

proof.claimBoundary: This covers the action grouping and reset request; final named-runtime visual inspection remains separate.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the official Hyperswitch action iframe isolated from document flow and give its provider-owned content a responsive viewport large enough for desktop and tablet controls.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Hyperswitch injects the official fullscreen iframe under a generated wrapper. The wrapper could retain flow dimensions, while the provider test page was squeezed into a narrow responsive breakpoint. A fixed zero-size mount prevents layout bleed; a centered dynamic viewport widens the official frame above 600px while mobile remains one viewport wide.

proof.claimBoundary: The test proves full dynamic viewport height, widened desktop viewport, no document-height growth, and zero root overflow. The nested provider page remains official cross-origin content and was not rewritten.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the ONSALE application shell pinned to the visible viewport so provider mount residue cannot expose the root document below it.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The shell was a normal-flow 100vh element. If an injected provider mount extended the outer document, scrolling could move the whole shell upward and reveal a large white root area. Only ONSALE app pages are now fixed to the dynamic viewport; the Flows document keeps normal scrolling.

proof.claimBoundary: The exact 1538 by 746 regression proves the shell is fixed at y=0, fills the viewport, and the provider overlay remains document-flow isolated. Payment, session, ticket, and Flows behavior are unchanged.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Expose the existing Buy Another Ticket reset action on Home for every saved checkout stage, not only fulfilled tickets.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: Checkout-ready and failure states could return Home with only Resume available, trapping a reviewer in the saved order. The banner now invokes the same guarded reset operation for all saved stages.

proof.claimBoundary: Checkout-ready and review-required Home banners expose Buy Another Ticket. The reset endpoint and payment, fulfillment, and ticket issuance logic are unchanged.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Give the official Hyperswitch iframe a wide CSS viewport so its own responsive Klarna and Affirm modal clears the narrow percentage-width breakpoint.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The provider-owned modal uses responsive percentage widths inside a cross-origin iframe. At the previous 1800 pixel cap its 2xl width remained about 486 pixels. A centered 2100 pixel CSS viewport yields at least 567 pixels for that provider breakpoint while ONSALE continues to isolate the iframe from document flow.

proof.claimBoundary: The merchant page proves a 2100 pixel official iframe viewport, full dynamic height, fixed flow isolation, and zero root overflow. The provider's cross-origin Tailwind markup cannot be rewritten by ONSALE and a real provider completion remains separate proof.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the official Hyperswitch provider action above the ONSALE document, fixed to the actual browser viewport, without a widened virtual canvas or document-flow residue.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The 2100 pixel virtual iframe viewport made the provider action non-responsive and contributed to the user-observed clipping and trailing document-space failure. The official frame now receives the real dynamic viewport and remains fixed outside normal layout.

proof.claimBoundary: The focused browser check proves a fixed viewport-sized official frame, hidden outer overflow, no document-height growth, and zero root horizontal overflow. Provider-owned content remains cross-origin and requires a separate live sandbox completion check.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the same-payment status check while exposing the existing Buy Another Ticket escape path when an official provider action is awaiting completion.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: A returned action-required checkout could present only status reconciliation, leaving a demo reviewer without an explicit fresh-session choice. The new action calls the existing reset boundary and does not alter confirmation, reconciliation, fulfillment, or ticket issuance.

proof.claimBoundary: The focused browser check proves the action-required status can return Home and issue the existing reset request. It does not claim to cancel an in-flight provider payment.

approvedExperienceDeltas.contract: Keep the action-required status controls compact, adjacent, and responsive without changing the checkout or provider overlay layout.
approvedExperienceDeltas.reason: The reset control belongs beside the existing same-payment status action, not in normal document flow or the provider overlay. The grouping preserves existing button styling and wraps only at narrow widths.

proof.claimBoundary: The focused browser check covers visible, operable controls. It does not claim cross-origin provider-content rendering.
